metadata.title: Solidian Pay Financial Technologies, Inc. — Unified Control Catalog
metadata.remarks: Fictional portfolio artifact. Controls are crosswalked to the AICPA SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria across all five categories (Security, Availability, Confidentiality, Processing Integrity, Privacy), and to ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, NIST AI RMF 1.0 and NIST CSF 2.0 — see props of class 'framework-mapping' on each control for the crosswalk, and props named 'soc2-category' for the Trust Services Criteria category each SOC 2 criterion belongs to. A reference is recorded only where the control itself satisfies it; controls are left unmapped against frameworks they do not address.

parts.name: statement

parts.name: guidance

parts.name: remarks

props.name: soc2-category
props.remarks: Trust Services Criteria category for A1.1

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Monitors and manages system capacity and availability against defined service commitments and SLOs for customer-facing payment and AI inference services; forecasts demand and provisions capacity ahead of it.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: SLO dashboards; capacity planning reviews; uptime reports against committed SLA

props.name: soc2-category
props.remarks: Trust Services Criteria category for CC9.1

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Identifies, selects and develops risk mitigation activities for risks arising from potential business disruptions, including maintenance of cyber liability and errors-and-omissions insurance appropriate to the risk profile, and assessment of concentration risk in critical vendors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Business disruption risk assessment; insurance policy schedule and renewal records; vendor concentration analysis; residual risk acceptance records

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: Insurance and vendor concentration analysis are the mitigation activities least visible in a technical control set, so they are tracked explicitly here

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintains a complete inventory of AI systems (internally built and third-party) with purpose, model type, and a risk-tiering method consistent with ISO 42001 and NIST AI RMF MAP function.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: AI system inventory; risk-tier assignment rationale; approval records

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: Inventory covers fraud scoring, underwriting, KYC review, support copilot, engineering copilot

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Pre-deployment and periodic assessment of AI systems for statistical bias, disparate impact, adversarial robustness, and safety failure modes, with defined risk-acceptance thresholds.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Fairness metric reports; adversarial test results; risk-acceptance sign-off

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: Fairness metrics defined for fraud and underwriting models; not yet extended to KYC review model

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensures human-in-the-loop or human-on-the-loop review is designed into AI systems commensurate with risk tier, with defined override authority and escalation paths.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Oversight model documentation; override logs; approval records

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: High-risk systems (fraud, underwriting) run HITL; low-risk engineering copilot runs unsupervised by design

parts.name: remarks

parts.name: statement

parts.name: guidance

parts.name: remarks

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dedicated intake, triage, and remediation path for AI-specific incidents (harmful/unsafe output, fairness violation, model compromise) distinct from generic IT incident handling.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: AI incident log; root-cause analyses; corrective action tracking

parts.name: remarks

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Assesses and documents the potential consequences of AI systems for individuals, groups of individuals, and society across the system life cycle. Assessments are performed before deployment, at planned intervals, and when significant changes are proposed; results are retained and feed risk treatment, human-oversight design, and the approval-to-deploy decision.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Impact assessment methodology and template; completed assessments per AI system; reviewer and approver sign-off; change-triggered reassessment log; assessment retention records

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: Impact assessment is the requirement that most distinguishes an AI management system from an information security one; template is defined but completed assessments exist only for the fraud scoring and underwriting models

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Ensures payment and ledger processing is complete, valid, accurate, timely and authorized: input validation and file-completeness checks at ingestion, automated exception queues for failed or suspended transactions, daily reconciliation between the processing ledger and settlement/bank records, and controlled correction of identified discrepancies with output delivered only to authorized recipients.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Daily reconciliation reports with sign-off; exception queue aging report; input validation rule set; settlement break log and resolution evidence; output distribution authorization matrix

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: For a payments company the completeness and accuracy of transaction processing is the core service commitment, so this control carries most of the Processing Integrity criteria

props.name: soc2-category
props.remarks: Trust Services Criteria category for CC3.3

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Formally considers the potential for fraud — both external transaction fraud and internal fraud/misappropriation — in assessing risks to objectives, including fraud scenarios arising from AI-assisted decisioning and from management override of controls.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Annual fraud risk assessment; fraud scenario register; management override monitoring evidence; fraud loss and attempted-fraud reporting

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: The AI fraud scoring model (AI-001) appears here as both a fraud control and a source of fraud risk, which is why management override and AI-assisted decisioning are explicit scenarios

props.name: soc2-category
props.remarks: Trust Services Criteria category for CC8.1

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Establishes rules for the secure development of software and systems: security requirements identified and approved for applications, documented secure architecture and engineering principles, secure coding standards enforced through peer review, automated security testing in CI (static analysis, dependency and secret scanning, infrastructure-as-code policy checks), and security acceptance testing before release. Applies to ML pipelines and model-serving code as well as application code.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Evidence required: Secure coding standard; security requirements and threat model records; CI scan reports (SAST, dependency, secret, IaC); code review records; pre-release security test sign-offs; test data handling procedure

parts.name: remarks
parts.prose: Static analysis and dependency scanning run in CI and the infrastructure-as-code checks are enforced by the Rego policies in policy/rego; threat modelling is not yet a standard step for every service
